evidence.title: Adelaide, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: Adelaide( died 1105), was sovereign Countess of Soissons from 1057 until 1105.

evidence.title: Adelaide, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: She was the daughter of Renaud I, Count of Soissons, and his wife, whose name is unknown, widow of Hilduin III, Count of Montdidier..

evidence.title: Adelaide, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: Adelaide became ruler of the County of Soissons upon the death of her father and brother, Guy II, Count of Soissons, in 1057.

evidence.title: Adelaide, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: Adelaide married William Busac, Count of Eu, grandson of Richard I, Duke of Normandy.

evidence.title: Adelaide, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: Adelaide and William had five children: William Busac became Count of Soissons," de jure uxoris", upon their marriage.

evidence.title: Theudebert of Soissons
evidence.text: Theudebert was the eldest son of King Chilperic I of Soissons, through his first wife Audovera.

evidence.title: Theudebert of Soissons
evidence.text: Theudebert was given command of Soissons in the early years of his father's reign.

evidence.title: Theudebert of Soissons
evidence.text: When his father precipitated a war with his brother Sigebert I of Austrasia, Sigebert marched on his capital and took the city, capturing and imprisoning Theudebert.

evidence.title: Theudebert of Soissons
evidence.text: He was out of prison a year later.

evidence.title: Theudebert of Soissons
evidence.text: On the death of King Charibert I of Paris in 567, Theudebert invaded Austrasia and razed many cities.

evidence.title: Theudebert of Soissons
evidence.text: In 575, Theudebert was killed in battle by Guntram Boso in the civil war between Chilperic, Sigbert, and Guntram, king of Burgundy.

evidence.title: Chilperic I
evidence.text: Chilperic I (c. 539 – September 584) was the king of Neustria (or Soissons) from 561 to his death.

evidence.title: Chilperic I
evidence.text: He was one of the sons of the Frankish king Clotaire I and Queen Aregund.

evidence.title: Margaret, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: Margaret (or Margaretha) of Soissons (died ca. 1350) was ruling Countess of Soissons in 1305-1344.

evidence.title: Margaret, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: She was the only daughter of Hugh, Count of Soissons, and Johanna of Argies.

evidence.title: Margaret, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: In 1306 she succeeded her father as Countess of Soissons.

evidence.title: Margaret, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text: Margaret was married to John of Beaumont, son of John II, Count of Holland.

evidence.title: Margaret, Countess of Soissons
evidence.text:
Margaret and John had five children:
Upon their marriage, John became Count of Soissons, "jure uxoris".

evidence.title: Guy II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Guy II( d. 1057), son of Renaud I, Count of Soissons, and his wife( name unknown), widow of Hilduin III, Count of Montdidier.

evidence.title: Guy II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Count of Soissons.

evidence.title: Guy II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Guy was identified as Count of Soissons in 1042 in a charter in which Gaunilo of Marmoutiers, the treasurer of St. Martin, denoted property.

evidence.title: Guy II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Guy died with his father in 1057 at the siege of Soissons.

evidence.title: Guy II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: It is not known whether or not Guy was married and no children are recorded.

evidence.title: Guy II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Upon his death, his sister Adelaide assumed the countship of Soissons.

evidence.title: Hannah Arnold
evidence.text: Hannah Arnold, also known as Hannah Waterman King, was the grandmother of Benedict Arnolds children.

evidence.title: Hubba bint Hulail
evidence.text: Hubba bint Hulail was the grandmother of Hashim ibn' Abd Manaf, thus the great- great- great- grandmother of the Islamic" Nabī"( Prophet) Muhammad ibn Abdullah.

evidence.title: Nocher II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Nocher II( d. 1019), Count of Bar- sur- Aube, Count of Soissons.

evidence.title: Nocher II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: He was the son of Nocher I, Count of Bar-sur- Aube.

evidence.title: Nocher II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Nocher ’s brother Beraud( d. 1052) was Bishop of Soissons.

evidence.title: Nocher II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Nocher became Count of Soissons, jure uxoris, upon his marriage to Adelise, Countess of Soissons.

evidence.title: Nocher II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Nocher and Adelisa had three children: Nocher ’s son and namesake became Count of Bar-sur- Aube upon his death, and the countship of Soissons reverted to his wife.

evidence.title: Nocher II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: His son Renaud would eventually become the Count of Soissons.

evidence.title: John V, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: John V( 21 March 1281 – 1304), son of John IV, Count of Soissons, and his wife Marguerite of Rumigny.

evidence.title: John V, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Count of Soissons.

evidence.title: John V, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: John inherited the countship of Soissons from his father in 1302.

evidence.title: John V, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Nothing is known about his brief rule of the county.

evidence.title: John V, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: He never married and died with no heirs.

evidence.title: John V, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Upon his death, his brother Hugh became Count of Soissons.

evidence.title: Renaud II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Renaud II( died 1099), son of William Busac, Count of Eu and Soissons, and Adelaide, Countess of Soissons.

evidence.title: Renaud II, Count of Soissons

evidence.title: Renaud II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: It is unclear when Renaud assumed the countship of Soissons from his disgraced father.

evidence.title: Renaud II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: The latter was stripped of the County of Eu in 1050 but it is unclear when he relinquished the countship of Soissons.

evidence.title: Renaud II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: Alberic of Trois- Fontaines identifies Renaud in his" Chronicles" but little is known about his rule.

evidence.title: Renaud II, Count of Soissons
evidence.text: It is not known whether Renaud married or had any children.

evidence.title: Renaud II, Count of Soissons
